newsitem.title: USA: Orange Cty, Calif., board considers airport plan.
newsitem.headline: Orange Cty, Calif., board considers airport plan.

text.p: The Orange County, Calif., Board of Supervisors on Wednesday was expected to vote on a plan to build a commercial airport at the El Toro Marine Corps Air Station.

After hearing public comments until late Tuesday, the board decided to reconvene Wednesday to take up the three reuse options -- a commercial passenger and cargo airport, a commercial cargo and general aviation airport, and non-aviation use.
After the vote, further environmental studies would be conducted. That process could take years, officials said.
The base is scheduled to be converted to civilian use by 1999.
Earlier this year, a study on future uses of the El Toro base concluded that converting the station into an international airport would pump nearly $10 billion a year into the area's economy.
The draft environmental impact report found that an international airport facility that could serve more than 38 million passengers a year would cost $1.6 billion to build.
The airport plan has sparked controversy in Orange County.
On Tuesday, the newly-formed Orange County Business Coalition, representing more than 50 local business leaders, questions the economic viability of the proposed El Toro international airport.
The group said the adverse environmental conditions created by the proposed airport could jeopardize the future economic growth of the surrounding areas.

"The Orange County business community, despite what airport proponents would have you believe, is not united in favor of the El Toro airport," said Laurie Casey, Orange County Business Coalition spokesperson.

"On behalf of prominent Orange County businesses, the coalition has deep-rooted concerns with both the airport and the planning process, as executed thus far. The Orange County Board of Supervisors has not given full attention to non-aviation alternatives," Casey said.
